title: Getting Started with xpam
text: xpam package builds geographic presence-absence matrices (PAMs) species range polygons. PAM sites--species binary table rows grid cells columns species; cell contains 1 species range overlaps cell 0 otherwise. PAMs fundamental data structure macroecology biogeography, used computing species richness, range-diversity plots, co-occurrence analyses, input conservation-prioritisation algorithms.

title: Getting Started with xpam
code: # From CRAN install.packages("xpam")  # Development version (identical code to the public repository) # install.packages("remotes") # remotes::install_github("alrobles/xpam")

title: Getting Started with xpam
text: core workflow two steps: Load species range polygons terra::SpatVector. Call get_geo_pam() desired grid resolution. result tibble. first two columns (x, y) cell centroids; remaining columns species, coded 1/0.
code: library(xpam)  # Step 1: load example data (Rodentia of Mexico) shp <- get_rodentia_mexico() shp  # Step 2: build the PAM at 1-degree resolution pam_result <- get_geo_pam(shp, res = 1) head(pam_result)

title: Getting Started with xpam
text: res argument controls grid cell size units CRS (decimal degrees EPSG:4326): Higher resolution → grid cells → finer spatial detail.
code: # Fine resolution (0.5 degree ~ 55 km at the equator) pam_fine <- get_geo_pam(shp, res = 0.5) dim(pam_fine)  # Coarse resolution (2 degrees ~ 220 km) pam_coarse <- get_geo_pam(shp, res = 2) dim(pam_coarse)

title: Getting Started with xpam
text: PAM, species richness per cell just row sum:
code: pam_result$richness <- rowSums(pam_result[, -(1:2)])  # Quick map with base R plot(pam_result$x, pam_result$y,      cex  = sqrt(pam_result$richness) * 0.3,      pch  = 15,      col  = hcl.colors(max(pam_result$richness))[pam_result$richness],      xlab = "Longitude",      ylab = "Latitude",      main = "Rodentia Species Richness — Mexico")

title: Getting Started with xpam
text: package also provides WorldClim PCA raster environmental analyses:
code: world_pca <- get_world_pca() terra::plot(world_pca)

title: Getting Started with xpam
text: get_geo_pam() builds raster memory, meant small inputs. continent- global-scale work package provides streaming native engine (C++17, OpenMP, GDAL): rasterises geometries bins occurrence records straight disk never materialises dense matrix. engine driven three functions. share occurrence source (occ, occ_file occ_polygons) raster inputs (env_files): pam_env_engine() returns marginals – richness per bin footprint per species; pam_incidence() returns PAM sparse matrix; pam_jaccard() computes species--species (site--site) Jaccard similarity incidence. geographic space pass space = "geo": env_files supplies grid geometry units terra cell numbers. engine built scale, resource limits explicit rather silent: max_bitset_mb caps shared bitset, max_out_mb caps size incidence may marshalled back R, threads controls OpenMP parallelism (OMP_THREAD_LIMIT respected). GDAL optional. has_gdal() reports whether installed build ; , engine functions stop informative error terra-based dense path keeps working.
code: # Environmental PAM marginals straight from raster files eng <- pam_env_engine(   env_files    = c("bio01.tif", "bio12.tif"),   occ_polygons = "ranges.gpkg",   poly_field   = "sciname",   nbs          = c(30, 30) ) eng$richness   # species per environmental bin eng$footprint  # bins occupied per species # The PAM itself, as a sparse units x species matrix inc <- pam_incidence(   env_files    = c("bio01.tif", "bio12.tif"),   occ_polygons = "ranges.gpkg",   poly_field   = "sciname",   space        = "env",   format       = "dgCMatrix" ) dim(inc$pam) # Pairwise Jaccard between species, from the same incidence jac <- pam_jaccard(   env_files    = c("bio01.tif", "bio12.tif"),   occ_polygons = "ranges.gpkg",   poly_field   = "sciname",   space        = "env" ) dim(jac$jaccard) # Geographic PAM: raster cells as units, ranges rasterised on the fly geo <- pam_incidence(   env_files    = "template.tif",   occ_polygons = "ranges.gpkg",   poly_field   = "sciname",   space        = "geo" ) geo$nnz

title: Getting Started with xpam
text: can pass terra::SpatVector sciname column: unique value sciname becomes column output PAM.
code: library(terra)  my_shapes <- vect("path/to/my_ranges.shp") names(my_shapes) # [1] "sciname" "family" "order"  ...  my_pam <- get_geo_pam(my_shapes, res = 0.25)

what: Presence-Absence Matrix Construction from Species Range Maps
title: Presence-Absence Matrix Construction from Species Range Maps
text: xpam builds presence-absence matrices (PAMs) species range polygons occurrence records. PAM sites--species binary table: rows sites (raster cells environmental bins), columns species, entry 1 (present) 0 (absent). PAMs foundational data structure macroecology biogeography computing species richness, range-diversity plots, co-occurrence analysis, conservation prioritisation. package offers two scales operation: dense small-input path (get_geo_pam()) rasterises terra::SpatVector onto grid returns tibble; streaming native engine (C++17, OpenMP, GDAL optional) never materialises dense matrix — pam_incidence() returns sparse PAM, pam_env_engine() returns marginals, pam_jaccard() computes species- site-wise Jaccard similarity directly incidence. Proven 22.5e9 occurrence pairs.

title: Presence-Absence Matrix Construction from Species Range Maps
text: GDAL optional. present build time (has_gdal() reports ) native raster engine links streams vector sources directly; without GDAL package still installs terra-based path works.
code: # From CRAN install.packages("xpam")  # Development version from GitHub # install.packages("remotes") remotes::install_github("alrobles/xpam")

title: Presence-Absence Matrix Construction from Species Range Maps
text: fully local example needs download:
code: library(xpam)  # Load example data: Rodentia of Mexico (downloaded on demand) shp <- get_rodentia_mexico()  # Build a PAM at 1-degree resolution pam_result <- get_geo_pam(shp, res = 1) head(pam_result) #> # A tibble: 6 × 42 #>       x     y Chaetodipus arenarius ... #>   <dbl> <dbl>                 <dbl> #> 1 -118.  23.5                     0 #> ... square <- function(x0, y0, size = 2) {   m <- matrix(c(x0, y0, x0 + size, y0,                 x0 + size, y0 + size, x0, y0 + size),               ncol = 2, byrow = TRUE)   terra::vect(m, type = "polygons", crs = "EPSG:4326") } ranges <- rbind(square(0, 0), square(2, 2)) ranges$sciname <- c("species_a", "species_b") get_geo_pam(ranges, res = 1)

title: Build a Presence-Absence Matrix from Species Range Polygons — get_geo_pam
code: # \donttest{ # A small, fully local example: two square ranges, no download needed square <- function(x0, y0, size = 2) {   m <- matrix(c(x0, y0, x0 + size, y0,                 x0 + size, y0 + size, x0, y0 + size),               ncol = 2, byrow = TRUE)   terra::vect(m, type = "polygons", crs = "EPSG:4326") } ranges <- rbind(square(0, 0), square(2, 2)) ranges$sciname <- c("species_a", "species_b") pam <- get_geo_pam(ranges, res = 1) head(pam) #> # title: xpam 0.3.0

title: xpam 0.3.0
text: New pam_env_engine(): builds environmental PAM straight raster files. PamEngine C++ object (opaque XPtr) owns GDAL /O computation; R passes paths, (species, cell) table scalars. Full-width strips read pixel-major buffer, cell binned GridBinning, pairs – pre-sorted cell – merge-join strips single pass PamBitset. Memory O(bitset + strip); max_bitset_mb triggers sort fallback pam_env(). Requires GDAL build time (has_gdal() reports ); configure degrades gracefully without . Raster cells terra cellnumbers (1-based). PamBitset rows word-aligned (<= 63 pad bits per species), pairwise kernels popcount(& B)/popcount(| B) per row pair via row() accessor. Parallel regions honour OMP_THREAD_LIMIT (via pam::safe_threads()); CRAN check machines set 2 omp_get_max_threads() alone respect .

title: xpam 0.3.0
text: occ: data frame (cell, species) — SEXP-anchored, sorted (MemOccSource). occ_file: cell-sorted “XPOC” binary pair file streamed ~48 MiB chunks (FileOccSource); xpam_write_occ_bin() writes . 4e6 cells x 500 species streamed path cuts RSS ~3.1 GB ~0.6 GB. path (shapefile, GeoPackage, GeoJSON, … OGR connection string duckdb:///db.duckdb GDAL build driver), character vector paths, directory scanned vector files — per-dataset cell-sorted streams k-way merged deduplicated (MergeOccSource); species required, -memory terra::SpatVector (bridged temporary GeoPackage). poly_layer takes one name per dataset single name applied ; all_touched selects burn rule; occ_dump tees stream engine consumes — merged deduplicated — reusable XPOC file (DumpOccSource). Polygon SRS reprojected env raster CRS differ; features missing/unmatched fields unusable geometries counted reported via n_skipped (+ warning).

title: xpam 0.3.0
text: New pam_incidence(): PAM R object. Streams occurrence source engine returns units x species incidence Matrix::dgCMatrix (format = "dgCMatrix", Matrix Suggests) raw data.frame(, j) triplet table. space = "geo" streaming geographic PAM (raster cells units, env files grid template — scalable replacement get_geo_pam()); space = "env" gives environmental incidence bins pam_env_engine(). Explicit scale gates: incidence export needs bitmap sort accumulator (geo co-occurrence path retains pairs), nnz * 16 B must fit max_out_mb marshal R — beyond -disk XPOC occ_dump sparse PAM.

title: xpam 0.3.0
text: pam_jaccard(): pairwise Jaccard similarity species straight occurrence source — dense PAM, RcppParallel. space = "geo" uses raster cells incidence units (env_files supplies grid template); space = "env" uses env bins. Accumulator: shared bitset n_species * n_units/8 fits max_bitset_mb; geo space beyond budget O(n_species^2) co-occurrence matrix accumulated per-cell species runs cell-sorted pair stream (kernel = "cooc", counts returned cooc). Semantics port fastJaccard::jaccard_fast: J = |&B| / ||B|, independence expectation pa*pb/(pa+pb-pa*pb) empty unions, centered = TRUE subtracts expectation. pam_jaccard(threshold = tau) returns similarity graph instead matrix: exact prefix-filtered join (AllPairs-style — rare-first prefix indexing, size count bounds, exact merge-join verification) emits edges data.frame (, j, J >= tau) output-sensitive work. results filtering dense matrix; works modes accumulators. 2,000-species x 20k-cell fixture ~80-280x faster fastJaccard’s dense RcppParallel path needs 305 MB input matrix (benchmarks/docs/bench_jaccard.md). pam_jaccard(= "site") transposes question: n_units x n_units matrix similarities cells env bins species share. Requires transposed bitset within max_bitset_mb dense n_units^2 return within max_out_mb (default 4096 MB, ~22.6k units).

title: xpam 0.3.0
text: Package renamed pam -> xpam: name pam already taken CRAN. Headers live src/*.h (.hpp) R CMD check flags unlikely file names src/ WARNING. Internal refactor: kernel’s heavy state moved pure-C++ headers (pam_bitset.h, pam_binning.h, pam_accumulate.h, pam_threads.h) Rcpp dependency; SystemRequirements raised C++17. New c_bin_assign_d(): D-dimensional grid binning matrix. pam_env() gains max_bitset_mb memory budget reports kernel used; accumulation fills single shared bitset lock-free atomic ORs; --range (species, bin) codes counted warned. xpam_sim_env() / xpam_sim_ranges() / xpam_truth() / xpam_niche_bound(): internal deterministic generators transparent R-oracle used validate engine (test-pam_sim.R). configure hardened: LIBS cleared probing GDAL link test uses gdal-config --libs, ambient environment libraries (e.g. user ~/.R/Makevars exporting -lRcppParallel R CMD INSTALL’s environment) can longer silently disable GDAL. AC_PROG_CXX also resolved link test instead lazily inside . Fixed url_exists() returning TRUE unresolvable hosts. Benchmarks: benchmarks/docs/bench_engine.md (incl. 1/120-degree global sweep: 22.5e9 pairs streamed, ~15-24 GB RSS) benchmarks/docs/bench_jaccard.md.
